audit_scope.description: This batch predominantly covers EL logic: EVM precompiles (ALT_BN128), storage operations (SLOAD/SSTORE/TLOAD/TSTORE), gas economics, transaction validation, exception handling, DELEGATECALL execution, nonce limits, and node record validation. EIP-2700 covers provider-level API interactions. EIP-778 covers P2P networking ENR records.

in_scope: EVM Opcodes (SLOAD, SSTORE, TLOAD, TSTORE, DELEGATECALL)

el_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions, resource exhaustion attacks, calldata bloat, nonce manipulation
Eclipse attacks, send invalid blocks/transactions, malformed ENR records, DNS poisoning for node discovery

el_vectors.entry_point: EVM Execution (CALL/DELEGATECALL to precompiles or storage)
el_vectors.threat: Crafted inputs to precompiles, gas manipulation via storage access patterns, reentrancy via DELEGATECALL
Inject malicious state change objects to execute unauthorized fund transfers or code deployments

cl_vectors.threat: Propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations (slashing condition), censorship

cl_vectors.entry_point: External APIs (e.g., MEV-Boost relay, checkpoint sync endpoint)
cl_vectors.threat: Provide incorrect data, censorship, denial of service

misclassified_entities.reason: Node operator controls the local node and is not an external entity sending data into the system from outside the trust boundary. The node operator is the system administrator.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any user or application can submit transactions via unauthenticated JSON-RPC. All transaction data (nonce, gas, calldata, signatures) must be fully validated. Covers EIP-7675 nonce/gas limits, EIP-8007 calldata pricing, and exception handling paths.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes on the P2P network are unauthenticated and potentially malicious. They can send invalid blocks, malformed transactions, or crafted data. All received blocks and transactions must pass full validation (InvalidBlock, InvalidTransaction exceptions).

trusted_external_entities.name: Calling Contract via EVM CALL/STATICCALL
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EVM precompile interface (ALT_BN128 add/mul/pairing at addresses 0x06-0x08)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any smart contract can invoke precompiles with arbitrary input bytes. Input validation (length, field element range, on-curve check, subgroup order) must be performed. Malformed inputs must result in OutOfGasError.

trusted_external_entities.name: Filesystem via SCO File Loading
trusted_external_entities.rationale: SCO files loaded from filesystem are potentially tampered with. Script verification, block height validation, and wallet isolation checks are required before trusting any recovery actions. Filesystem access is unauthenticated.

trusted_external_entities.name: DNS Discovery Service
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: DNS TXT records containing ENR data (EIP-778)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DNS infrastructure is subject to spoofing and cache poisoning. ENR records from DNS must have cryptographic signature validation before use. DNS provides no authentication of content.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via ENR Exchange
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P ENR record exchange (EIP-778 node discovery)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote peers can send crafted ENR records. Size limits (300 bytes), RLP structure validation, key ordering, identity scheme verification, and cryptographic signature checks are required.

trusted_external_entities.name: ENS Registry via Name Resolution
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: ENS name resolution returning ENR records (EIP-778)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: ENS data depends on on-chain integrity but could be manipulated by contract owners. ENR records from ENS must still pass full cryptographic validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Client DApp via Provider API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Client applications interact with the injected provider through the event listener API. Applications are untrusted web content that could register excessive listeners or manipulate event subscriptions.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet Extension via Provider Injection
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Wallet extensions inject provider objects into web pages. A malicious extension could inject a fake provider that emits false events or intercepts calls. The provider controls all event data passed to listeners.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Transaction validation pipeline (nonce, signature, gas, balance checks)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: signature verification (InvalidSignatureError), sender authorization (InvalidSenderError), nonce matching (NonceMismatchError), nonce overflow check (NonceOverflowError), intrinsic gas coverage (InsufficientTransactionGasError), block gas limit (GasUsedExceedsLimitError), sender balance (InsufficientBalanceError), gas limit cap 2^63-1 (EIP-4803), reject code senders (EIP-3607).

Full block validation required. Invalid blocks must raise InvalidBlock exception and be rejected. Empty account state violations must raise StateWithEmptyAccount. All contained transactions must pass individual validation.

Input length validation (64 bytes for G1, 128 bytes for G2, multiple of 192 for pairing). Field element range check (< field modulus). Point-on-curve verification. Subgroup order validation for pairing. Gas charging before computation (150 for add, 6000 for mul, 34000*n+45000 for pairing). All failures must result in OutOfGasError.

Input must be validated as multiple of 192 bytes. Each G1+G2 pair must pass individual point validation and subgroup order check. Invalid curve attacks must be prevented through subgroup membership verification.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: SCO file loading at client startup (EIP-867)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: SCO files must pass script safety audit (no unsafe operations), block height must be hardcoded for reproducibility, no unlocked wallets during verification. File integrity must be ensured. Malicious SCO files could execute unauthorized state changes.
All SCO files must be treated as untrusted until passing script audit, block height verification, and wallet isolation checks. Failed verification must result in SCO rejection.

ENR records from DNS must pass: size limit check (<=300 bytes), RLP decoding, key ordering validation, identity scheme extraction, and cryptographic signature verification. DNS spoofing is mitigated by signature validation but could still cause DoS via invalid records.
Same validation as DNS-sourced ENRs. Peer-provided ENR data is binary RLP-encoded and must pass all validation steps. Sequence number comparison required for freshness.
ENS-sourced ENRs must pass same cryptographic validation. ENS data integrity depends on on-chain state, but ENR signatures provide independent verification.
Provider must handle duplicate listener registration safely. Listener removal must correctly decrease callback count. No resource exhaustion from excessive listener registration.

Provider injection assumes legitimate wallet extension. Malicious providers could emit fake events (accountsChanged, chainChanged) to trick applications. Applications should verify provider authenticity.
